speaker: system
text: On the last night of autumn, a mapmaker walked into a valley that was not on any of her maps.

speaker: vesper
text: (Eleven days out of Harrowmere. Two of them on a road my own survey says is a river.)

speaker: vesper
text: (There are lights up ahead. Lights mean somebody who can tell me where I am.)

speaker: vesper
text: (A waystone. Good — the road's a real road, then.)

speaker: vesper
text: (…Wait.)

speaker: vesper
text: (I've drawn this stone. This exact stone — the face, the crack through its chin.)

speaker: vesper
text: (It's in my sketchbook right now. And I have never been here in my life.)

speaker: mochi
text: Mrrp.

speaker: vesper
text: GAH— …a cat. Hello. Don't sneak up on people in haunted forests.

speaker: mochi
text: Mrrp.

speaker: vesper
text: There are lights up the road. Come on. If anyone can explain my sketchbook, it's whoever lives here.

speaker: system
text: The wood thinned, and there was an arch with harvest wreaths on it, and past the arch a square full of lamplight and people.

speaker: vesper
text: (A festival. Of course. I arrive somewhere for the first time in my life and it's the one night they're all outside.)

speaker: vesper
text: (That warmth is not weather. I have been cold for eleven days and I stopped being cold at the arch.)

speaker: vesper
text: (Right. Somebody here knows what a gate on my chart is doing in a valley that isn't.)

speaker: rowan
text: Now then! A guest, and on Emberwake of all nights. Welcome, my dear.

speaker: vesper
text: Vesper. Mapmaker. I need to get through your gate, and I'm told you're in charge.

speaker: rowan
text: In charge! Ha! I keep the ledger; the village keeps itself.

speaker: rowan
text: And nobody opens the Old Gate, child. It hasn't a key — it has RULES.

speaker: vesper
text: Rules can be charted. Charting things is my whole profession.

speaker: rowan
text: …Ha! I like you. Stay the night, then — and stay for the Kindling Hour.

speaker: rowan
text: Three hundred years that flame has burned. In all of them, nobody here carried a grief alone.

speaker: rowan
text: That is not boasting, my dear. It is bookkeeping — I checked.

speaker: rowan
text: As for the Gate — lamplighter business, child. His order built it, his order shut it.

speaker: rowan
text: Ask HIM. The quiet one with the flame that never goes out.

speaker: rowan
text: You'll find him somewhere across the village, apologizing to lamps.

speaker: vesper
text: Apologizing to lamps.

speaker: rowan
text: Ha! You'll see.

speaker: vesper
text: Excuse me. You look official — you're holding fire.

speaker: vesper
text: Are you the lamplighter, or do I keep collecting cats until one talks?

speaker: lake
text: Oh. Um. Yes? The first one. Lake. The cats don't talk, to my knowledge.

speaker: vesper
text: Vesper. Mapmaker.

speaker: lake
text: I know. Poppy's told half the square about you.

speaker: vesper
text: Your elder says the Old Gate is your family's business, and I need it open.

speaker: lake
text: The— nobody crosses the Gate. It hasn't opened in my lifetime.

speaker: vesper
text: Because this valley isn't on any chart I own. And I walked here anyway.

speaker: vesper
text: Something on the other side of that gate has been sending me MAIL, Lake. I intend to answer it in person.

speaker: lake
text: …what?

speaker: lake
text: Ask me after. Three lamps left, and the ring closes before full dark — that's the order she gave me.

speaker: lake
text: (One. While this lamp burns, every house on the lane sits inside the village's heart. Dark lamp, dull street.)

speaker: vesper
text: …You're apologizing to it.

speaker: lake
text: It's been a long year for the lane.

speaker: lake
text: Two more, up in the square. Walk with me.

speaker: lake
text: (Two. “Light them like you mean it,” she said, “or they gutter by midnight.”)

speaker: lake
text: (She never once explained what the meaning involved. I improvise.)

speaker: lake
text: (Three. The ring is closed before full dark, same as every night of my life.)

speaker: lake
text: (A lit lamp near every door. Now the Hour can start.)

speaker: rowan
text: The HOUR! Gather, neighbors — to the square!

speaker: rowan
text: Lake — the flame.

speaker: rowan
text: Neighbors! The year turns!

speaker: rowan
text: Three hundred years, and the warmth of every one of them — right here.

speaker: rowan
text: You know the trade. Bring the year's best, and tell it to the flame.

speaker: rowan
text: You keep the memory — every minute, yours till you die. The flame keeps the WARMTH, and shines it on all of us, for good.

speaker: rowan
text: Who brings the first memory?

speaker: poppy
text: The flood! The spring flood — the whole town in my bakery, bailing water with soup pots, and LAUGHING, gods help us—

speaker: pip
text: This is the BEST night.

speaker: pip
text: …Why did the music stop?

speaker: system
text: It did not happen slowly. Between one heartbeat and the next, the light of Emberbrook — three hundred years of it — stood up and left.

speaker: system
text: Moths came off the Heartlight the way sparks come off a struck flint, and did not climb, and did not go anywhere.

speaker: poppy
text: …My stall. My bread. Why doesn't any of it feel like MINE?

speaker: pip
text: Mama?

speaker: mara
text: …I'm sorry — whose child— no. I know whose. Mine.

speaker: mara
text: I can say it, and it weighs NOTHING— someone's crying. Why is someone crying?

speaker: pip
text: Mama. It's me, it's Pip. You KNOW me!

speaker: rowan
text: Everyone stay where you are. Names! Say your names, out loud — say them NOW.

speaker: rowan
text: …I know my name. It just doesn't feel like mine to say.

speaker: lake
text: Rowan. Your name is Rowan.

speaker: vesper
text: …You know them? All of them?

speaker: lake
text: Every window in this village. Every name behind it.

speaker: rowan
text: You two. The stranger and the lamplighter. Everyone in this square is a stranger wearing a neighbor's face — except you.

speaker: vesper
text: I got here an HOUR ago.

speaker: lake
text: And keepers don't make tellings. We keep our own — Grandmother's one hard rule.

speaker: lake
text: …My lighter's still warm. Every other flame in Emberbrook just died — not this one.

speaker: rowan
text: Then we are not finished. Not yet.

speaker: rowan
text: See to them — all of them. They deserve their names back, even borrowed.

speaker: rowan
text: Then come find me. I will be with my ledger — every word of it true, and not one of them mine.

speaker: poppy
text: …My stall. My bread. My hands — I know every burn scar on them. Why does none of it feel like MINE?

speaker: lake
text: You're Poppy. You bake.

speaker: lake
text: Every morning you burn your thumb on the first tray, and swear you won't tomorrow.

speaker: poppy
text: …Do I do it anyway?

speaker: lake
text: Every morning.

speaker: poppy
text: The round warm things. I know the word — it just sounds like nobody's when I say it.

speaker: poppy
text: Say it to me, love.

speaker: vesper
text: Honeybuns.

speaker: poppy
text: HONEYBUNS. Say more words. Both of you.

speaker: vesper
text: I'm writing this down. All of it — who you are, and who you are to each other.

speaker: poppy
text: Good, love. Write the thumb. The thumb feels true.

speaker: pip
text: Tell her. TELL her!

speaker: lake
text: Mara. This is Pip. Your son, seven years old.

speaker: lake
text: You waited out a snowstorm at the pass for him to be born.

speaker: mara
text: I believe you. That is the worst of it — every word lands like a fact about a stranger.

speaker: pip
text: …You held my hand. TONIGHT. You said I'd remember tonight forever.

speaker: vesper
text: Pip. Look at me. I saw her holding your hand — an hour ago, by the stall.

speaker: vesper
text: I'm a mapmaker. I keep records of true things.

speaker: vesper
text: So I am telling you: it is TRUE.

speaker: vesper
text: It happened, and I have it.

speaker: pip
text: …Is it in ink?

speaker: vesper
text: It is now.

speaker: mara
text: Whoever you two are — whatever you still carry — do not waste it. Please.

speaker: finn
text: My name… I can say the word, friend. It just isn't MINE anymore.

speaker: finn
text: Hands still know the knots, though. Funny what stays.

speaker: lake
text: Finn. You're Finn.

speaker: finn
text: …Finn. Huh. Short. I like it.

speaker: finn
text: One thing for your book, mapmaker. The fish stopped circlin' the moment it happened.

speaker: finn
text: Like they'd been countin' down to it.

speaker: vesper
text: Fish don't count.

speaker: finn
text: Didn't think so either. This morning I was wrong about a lot of things.

speaker: vesper
text: The cat. The cat is FINE?!

speaker: system
text: (Mochi is purring. Mochi has, if anything, improved.)

speaker: lake
text: Cats don't keep their hearts where moths can reach. My grandmother used to say that.

speaker: vesper
text: Your grandmother said that. Casually. As common knowledge.

speaker: lake
text: She said a lot of things. She was a lamplighter too.

speaker: system
text: (He is watching the north road. He does not usually watch anything.)

speaker: rowan
text: Look at this. The year four-twenty-nine. The flood. A wedding.

speaker: rowan
text: I wrote every line of this page — and tonight I read it like the minutes of somebody else's village.

speaker: rowan
text: Ink keeps facts. It cannot keep what they WEIGHED.

speaker: rowan
text: Our flame was first drawn from a shrine deep in the Whisperwood. The Kindling.

speaker: rowan
text: And the old Order kept one creed above all: light does not die — it is only ever carried.

speaker: rowan
text: Whatever THAT was tonight, it did not put our flame out, children. It carried it off. Whole.

speaker: lake
text: Nobody knows the way. The Gate's been shut three hundred years, and the road's gone.

speaker: vesper
text: …I need to show you both something, and I need you to not be strange about it.

speaker: vesper
text: Since I was six years old, I have drawn one clearing. Over and over, in dreams.

speaker: vesper
text: Forty-one drawings of the same clearing.

speaker: vesper
text: I came here because the forty-first had YOUR gate in the corner.

speaker: rowan
text: Girl… that is the Kindling. That is the heart of the Whisperwood.

speaker: rowan
text: It has been CALLING you. Forty-one times it called.

speaker: rowan
text: The map does not know fire. The flame does not know the way.

speaker: rowan
text: So it must be both of you, together.

speaker: vesper
text: We met an hour ago.

speaker: rowan
text: Then you have an hour's head start on resenting each other. Marvelous.

speaker: rowan
text: Understand what you carry, boy. That little flame is the last live fire in the valley.

speaker: lake
text: I'm scared to walk that road, and I'll walk it. Both of those are true.

speaker: rowan
text: The old rite, then. Two keepers, one flame — say it and mean it, or the Gate will know.

speaker: rowan
text: “What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.”

speaker: vesper
text: What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.

speaker: lake
text: What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.

speaker: rowan
text: …The cat is going with you.

speaker: lake
text: He's not my—

speaker: rowan
text: It was not a question, boy.

speaker: rowan
text: That cat has been watching the north road all evening. Take the hint.

speaker: rowan
text: Twin sigils, before the Gate. The Lamplighters cut them, in the old days.

speaker: rowan
text: That road was always meant to be walked by two.
